patterns.name: Arrays & Hashing
patterns.short_description: The foundation every other pattern builds on: storing and looking up values in O(1) with hash maps/sets, and manipulating arrays in place.
patterns.when_to_use: Almost any problem involving 'have I seen this before', frequency counting, grouping by a computed key, or needing O(1) average lookup instead of scanning.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'duplicate', 'frequency', 'count of', 'group by', 'anagram'. If brute force is O(n^2) because of a nested 'does this exist elsewhere' check, a hash map usually gets it to O(n).
patterns.complexity: O(n) time, O(n) space for a hash map/set pass, versus O(n^2) time / O(1) space for the nested-loop brute force.

problems.name: Contains Duplicate
problems.hint: Put elements in a set; if the set doesn't grow, you found a duplicate.

problems.name: Valid Anagram
problems.hint: Count character frequencies in both strings and compare the maps.

problems.name: Two Sum
problems.hint: Hash map of value -> index; check for the complement as you scan once.

problems.name: Group Anagrams
problems.hint: Sorted-string (or char-count tuple) as the hash map key groups anagrams together.

problems.name: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.hint: Count frequencies with a hash map, then bucket sort by frequency for O(n).

problems.name: Product of Array Except Self
problems.hint: Two passes: prefix products from the left, suffix products from the right.

problems.name: Valid Sudoku
problems.hint: A set per row, column, and 3x3 box to track seen digits.

problems.name: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.hint: Put all values in a set; only start counting a streak from a number with no predecessor.

problems.name: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.hint: Hash map of prefix-sum -> count; check if (prefix_sum - k) has been seen.

problems.name: First Missing Positive
problems.hint: Place each value at its 'correct' index in-place (cyclic placement) using the array itself as a hash set.

patterns.name: Two Pointers
patterns.short_description: Use two indices moving through a sequence (from ends inward, or both forward at different speeds) to avoid nested loops.
patterns.when_to_use: Sorted arrays/strings where you need pairs/triplets satisfying a condition, in-place partitioning, palindrome checks, or merging two sorted structures.
patterns.recognition_tips: Look for: sorted input, 'pair that sums to X', 'remove duplicates in place', palindrome checks, or merging two sorted arrays/lists. If a brute force is O(n^2) with nested loops scanning the same array, two pointers can often bring it to O(n).
patterns.complexity: Typically O(n) time (each pointer traverses the array at most once) and O(1) extra space, versus O(n^2) for the brute-force nested-loop equivalent.

problems.name: Valid Palindrome
problems.hint: Two pointers from both ends, skip non-alphanumeric, compare lowercase chars.

problems.name: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
problems.hint: Classic converge-from-ends pattern since the array is already sorted.

problems.name: Reverse String
problems.hint: Swap left/right pointers moving toward the middle, in place.

problems.name: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.hint: Slow pointer marks the write position, fast pointer scans for new unique values.

problems.name: Merge Sorted Array
problems.hint: Two pointers starting from the END of both arrays to avoid overwriting.

problems.name: 3Sum
problems.hint: Fix one element, then two-pointer the remaining sorted subarray for the other two.

problems.name: Container With Most Water
problems.hint: Move the pointer at the shorter line inward; it can never help to move the taller one.

problems.name: Sort Colors
problems.hint: Dutch National Flag: three pointers (low/mid/high) partitioning in one pass.

problems.name: 4Sum
problems.hint: Fix two elements with nested loops, then two-pointer the rest — generalizes 3Sum.

problems.name: Trapping Rain Water
problems.hint: Two pointers tracking left_max/right_max, always advancing the side with the smaller max.

patterns.name: Sliding Window
patterns.short_description: Maintain a contiguous 'window' over an array/string, expanding and shrinking its boundaries to track a running property (sum, count, distinct chars) without recomputation.
patterns.when_to_use: Subarray/substring problems asking for the longest/shortest/count of contiguous ranges satisfying a constraint (sum, distinct chars, frequency).
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords like 'contiguous subarray', 'substring', 'longest/shortest/max/min window', or 'at most K distinct'. If brute force tries every (i,j) pair and recomputes the window property from scratch, sliding window turns it into O(n).
patterns.complexity: O(n) time since each pointer moves forward at most n times total (amortized), O(k) space for a window's auxiliary hashmap/set.
patterns.template_code:
def sliding_window(s, k):
    window_start = 0
    state = {}  # e.g. character counts
    best = 0
    for window_end in range(len(s)):
        # 1. Expand: add s[window_end] into `state`
        right_char = s[window_end]
        state[right_char] = state.get(right_char, 0) + 1

        # 2. Shrink while window is invalid
        while not is_valid(state, k):
            left_char = s[window_start]
            state[left_char] -= 1
            if state[left_char] == 0:
                del state[left_char]
            window_start += 1

        # 3. Record best window size
        best = max(best, window_end - window_start + 1)
    return best

problems.hint: Fixed-size window: slide by subtracting the outgoing element and adding the incoming one.

problems.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock

problems.hint: Window valid while (window size - count of most frequent char) <= k replacements.

problems.hint: Fixed-size window equal to len(s1), compare frequency maps.

problems.hint: Variable window: expand until sum >= target, then shrink to minimize length.

problems.name: Sliding Window Maximum
problems.hint: Monotonic deque holding indices of window maxima as the fixed window slides.

problems.name: Minimum Window Substring
problems.hint: Variable window with a 'need' frequency map; shrink while still covering all needed chars.

patterns.name: Stacks & Queues (Fundamentals)
patterns.short_description: LIFO (stack) and FIFO (queue) as the base building blocks for matching/nesting problems, expression evaluation, and simulating processes in order.
patterns.when_to_use: Balanced-parentheses/nesting checks, expression parsing/evaluation, and any 'process things in the order they arrived (queue)' or 'undo the most recent thing (stack)' problem.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'valid parentheses', 'nested', 'evaluate expression', 'undo', 'most recent'. If you keep needing to look at 'the last thing I saw that isn't resolved yet', that's a stack.
patterns.complexity: O(n) time to push/process each element once, O(n) space for the stack/queue in the worst case.

problems.name: Valid Parentheses
problems.hint: Push opening brackets; on a closing bracket, pop and check it matches.

problems.name: Implement Queue using Stacks
problems.hint: Two stacks: one for enqueue, transfer to the other (reversing order) to dequeue.

problems.name: Implement Stack using Queues
problems.hint: Rotate the queue after each push so the newest element is always at the front.

problems.name: Min Stack
problems.hint: Keep a second stack tracking the running minimum alongside the main stack.

problems.name: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
problems.hint: Push operands; on an operator, pop two, apply it, push the result back.

problems.name: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String
problems.hint: Push chars; if the top matches the incoming char, pop instead of pushing.

problems.name: Design Circular Queue
problems.hint: Fixed-size array with head/tail indices wrapping via modulo.

problems.name: Decode String
problems.hint: Stack of (previous_string, repeat_count) pairs, pushed on '[' and combined on ']'.

problems.name: Basic Calculator II
problems.hint: Stack of pending terms; push/pop based on operator precedence (+ - vs * /).

problems.name: Basic Calculator
problems.hint: Stack to save (result, sign) when entering '(' and restore it on ')'.

patterns.name: Linked List (Fundamentals)
patterns.short_description: Core pointer-manipulation operations on singly/doubly linked lists: traversal, reversal, merging, and insertion/deletion — the basis for the more advanced Fast & Slow Pointers pattern.
patterns.when_to_use: Any direct linked-list manipulation: reversing all or part of a list, merging sorted lists, or inserting/deleting nodes given only a pointer.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'linked list', 'reverse', 'merge two lists', 'in-place' with O(1) extra space required (ruling out copying into an array).
patterns.complexity: O(n) time to traverse the list once, O(1) extra space for pointer-rewiring approaches (vs O(n) if you copy into an array).
patterns.template_code:
def reverse_linked_list(head):
    prev = None
    curr = head
    while curr:
        next_node = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = next_node
    return prev

problems.hint: Iteratively re-point each node's `next` to the previous node.

patterns.name: Fast & Slow Pointers
patterns.short_description: Two pointers traverse a linked list (or implicit sequence) at different speeds (usually 1x and 2x) to detect cycles, find midpoints, or find cycle entry points without extra space.
patterns.when_to_use: Linked list problems needing cycle detection, the middle node, or detecting cycles in an implicit functional graph (e.g. Happy Number, Find the Duplicate Number).
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'linked list', 'cycle', 'middle of the list', or a sequence defined by repeatedly applying a function to a number/index (which implies an implicit linked structure).
patterns.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space — the key advantage over using a hash set to detect visited nodes (which is O(n) space).

patterns.complexity: O(log n) time, O(1) space for the iterative form (O(log n) call stack if recursive).

patterns.name: Graphs — Advanced (Shortest Path & Topological Sort)
patterns.short_description: Beyond basic DFS/BFS: ordering nodes under dependency constraints (topological sort) and finding shortest paths in weighted graphs (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford style relaxation).
patterns.when_to_use: Scheduling with prerequisites/dependencies, weighted shortest-path queries, and problems needing a valid build/processing order.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'prerequisite', 'build order', 'shortest path', 'minimum cost to reach', 'at most K stops', weighted edges.
patterns.complexity: Topological sort: O(V + E). Dijkstra with a binary heap: O((V + E) log V). Bellman-Ford / K-stops relaxation: O(V * E) or O(K * E).
patterns.template_code:
import heapq
from collections import defaultdict, deque

def topological_sort(num_nodes, edges):
    graph = defaultdict(list)
    indegree = [0] * num_nodes
    for u, v in edges:  # u -> v
        graph[u].append(v)
        indegree[v] += 1
    queue = deque(n for n in range(num_nodes) if indegree[n] == 0)
    order = []
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        order.append(node)
        for nxt in graph[node]:
            indegree[nxt] -= 1
            if indegree[nxt] == 0:
                queue.append(nxt)
    return order if len(order) == num_nodes else []  # [] means a cycle exists

def dijkstra(num_nodes, graph, start):
    dist = [float('inf')] * num_nodes
    dist[start] = 0
    heap = [(0, start)]
    while heap:
        d, node = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if d > dist[node]:
            continue
        for neighbor, weight in graph[node]:
            nd = d + weight
            if nd < dist[neighbor]:
                dist[neighbor] = nd
                heapq.heappush(heap, (nd, neighbor))
    return dist

problems.hint: Kahn's algorithm (BFS topological sort): return the order, or [] if a cycle is detected.

problems.name: Minimum Height Trees
problems.hint: Repeatedly peel leaf nodes (BFS layer by layer) until 1-2 nodes remain — those are the centroids.

problems.name: Network Delay Time
problems.hint: Textbook Dijkstra from the source; answer is the max shortest-distance across all nodes.

problems.name: Path with Minimum Effort
problems.hint: Dijkstra-style relaxation where 'distance' is the max height-difference along the path, not a sum.

problems.name: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
problems.hint: Bellman-Ford limited to K relaxation rounds (or BFS/Dijkstra tracking stops used).

problems.name: Reconstruct Itinerary
problems.hint: Hierholzer's algorithm: greedy DFS using each ticket once, building the Eulerian path in reverse.

problems.name: Bus Routes
problems.hint: BFS over routes (not stops): each level switches to every route reachable from the current stops.

patterns.name: Heaps / Top-K
patterns.short_description: Maintain a min-heap or max-heap of size K to efficiently track the K largest/smallest/most-frequent elements without sorting the whole input.
patterns.when_to_use: 'Kth largest/smallest', 'top K frequent', merging K sorted lists, running median.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'Kth largest', 'top K', 'K closest', 'median of a stream'.
patterns.complexity: O(n log k) time to process n elements with a size-k heap, O(k) space.

problems.name: Last Stone Weight
problems.hint: Max-heap (negate values for Python's min-heap): repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones.

problems.name: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
problems.hint: Maintain a min-heap of size k; its top is always the current kth largest.

problems.name: K Closest Points to Origin
problems.hint: Max-heap of size k on distance, popping the farthest point whenever the heap overflows.

problems.name: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.hint: Min-heap of size k (or quickselect for average O(n)).

problems.name: Top K Frequent Words
problems.hint: Count frequencies, then a heap with a custom comparator (frequency desc, then lexicographic).

problems.name: Reorganize String
problems.hint: Max-heap by frequency; repeatedly place the two most frequent remaining characters.

problems.name: Ugly Number II
problems.hint: Min-heap seeded with 1, pushing num*2, num*3, num*5 for each popped ugly number (dedup with a set).

problems.name: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
problems.hint: Min-heap seeded with the smallest pairs, expanding neighbors as you pop the current smallest sum.

problems.name: IPO
problems.hint: Sort projects by capital needed; use a max-heap on profit for all currently affordable projects.

problems.name: Find Median from Data Stream
problems.hint: Two heaps (max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper half), kept balanced in size.

patterns.name: Greedy
patterns.short_description: Make the locally optimal choice at each step, proving (or trusting a known result) that local optimality leads to a global optimum.
patterns.when_to_use: Interval scheduling, jump-game reachability, assigning resources for max/min outcome — when an exchange argument shows greedy is safe.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'maximum number of', 'minimum number of', problems where sorting first reveals an obvious optimal order.
patterns.complexity: Usually O(n log n) (dominated by an initial sort), O(1) extra space.

problems.name: Assign Cookies
problems.hint: Sort both children's greed and cookie sizes; greedily satisfy the least-greedy child first.

problems.name: Boats to Save People
problems.hint: Sort weights; two pointers pairing the lightest with the heaviest when they fit together.

problems.name: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
problems.hint: Greedily capture every positive day-to-day price increase.

problems.name: Jump Game
problems.hint: Track the farthest reachable index greedily while scanning left to right.

problems.name: Jump Game II
problems.hint: Greedy BFS-by-levels: track the current jump's farthest reach and the next jump's farthest reach.

problems.name: Gas Station
problems.hint: If total gas >= total cost a solution exists; greedily restart the start index whenever the tank goes negative.

problems.name: Partition Labels
problems.hint: Greedily extend the current partition's end to the last occurrence of every character seen so far.

problems.name: Task Scheduler
problems.hint: Greedily schedule around the most frequent task, computing idle slots via a formula.

problems.name: Queue Reconstruction by Height
problems.hint: Sort tall-first, then insert each person at their k-index — taller people already placed don't move.

problems.name: Candy
problems.hint: Two greedy passes (left-to-right, then right-to-left) enforcing the 'more candy than a lower neighbor' rule.

patterns.name: Bit Manipulation
patterns.short_description: Use bitwise operators (AND, OR, XOR, shifts) to solve problems in O(1) per element with O(1) space, exploiting properties like XOR self-cancellation.
patterns.when_to_use: 'Find the single/missing number', counting set bits, subset generation via bitmask, power-of-two checks.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'without extra space', 'XOR', 'single number', 'power of two', bitmask DP over small n.
patterns.complexity: O(1) per bitwise op; overall usually O(n) time, O(1) space — much better than an O(n) space hashmap approach.

problems.name: Single Number
problems.hint: XOR every element; duplicates cancel out, leaving the single value.

problems.name: Number of 1 Bits
problems.hint: Repeatedly clear the lowest set bit with n & (n - 1), counting iterations.

problems.name: Counting Bits
problems.hint: DP: bits(i) = bits(i >> 1) + (i & 1).

problems.name: Missing Number
problems.hint: XOR all indices and all values together; everything cancels except the missing number.

problems.name: Reverse Bits
problems.hint: Shift bits out of the input from the right and into the result from the right, 32 times.

problems.name: Power of Two
problems.hint: A power of two has exactly one set bit: check n > 0 and (n & (n - 1)) == 0.

problems.name: Single Number II
problems.hint: Track bit counts mod 3 per bit position (or use two accumulator variables as a mod-3 counter).

problems.name: Single Number III
problems.hint: XOR everything to get a^b, use its lowest set bit to split nums into two groups, XOR each group.

problems.name: Sum of Two Integers
problems.hint: Simulate addition without + : XOR gives sum-without-carry, AND<<1 gives the carry; loop until carry is 0.

problems.name: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
problems.hint: Build numbers bit by bit greedily using a prefix trie (or hash set) of seen prefixes.

patterns.name: Dynamic Programming (1D)
patterns.short_description: Break a problem into overlapping subproblems indexed by a single dimension (e.g. position i), and build up the answer from a small base case using a recurrence, caching results to avoid recomputation.
patterns.when_to_use: Problems asking for a count/min/max over sequences where the answer at position i depends on answers at a small number of earlier positions (i-1, i-2, ...).
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'number of ways', 'minimum/maximum cost to reach', 'longest/shortest such that', on a 1D sequence (array/string) with optimal-substructure and overlapping subproblems. If a greedy or two-pointer approach provably fails on some case, DP is often the fallback.
patterns.complexity: Typically O(n) time and O(n) space (often reducible to O(1) space by keeping only the last few states), versus exponential O(2^n) for a naive recursive brute force without memoization.

problems.name: Climbing Stairs
problems.hint: dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2] — Fibonacci-shaped recurrence.

problems.name: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
problems.hint: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]).

problems.name: House Robber
problems.hint: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]) — take or skip the current house.

problems.name: Maximum Subarray
problems.hint: Kadane's algorithm: dp[i] = max(nums[i], dp[i-1] + nums[i]).

problems.name: House Robber II
problems.hint: Circular array: run House Robber twice, excluding first or last house, take the max.

problems.name: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.hint: dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) over all j < i with nums[j] < nums[i].

problems.name: Coin Change
problems.hint: dp[amount] = min number of coins; dp[a] = min(dp[a - coin] + 1) over all coins.

problems.name: Word Break
problems.hint: dp[i] = True if some dp[j] is True and s[j:i] is in the dictionary.

problems.name: Decode Ways
problems.hint: dp[i] combines dp[i-1] (single digit valid) and dp[i-2] (two-digit valid).

problems.name: Maximum Product Subarray
problems.hint: Track both running max AND min at each i, since a negative can flip min to max.

patterns.name: Dynamic Programming (2D / Knapsack)
patterns.short_description: Extend 1D DP to a 2D table dp[i][j] indexed by two dimensions (e.g. two sequences, or item index + remaining capacity).
patterns.when_to_use: String comparison (edit distance, LCS), grid path problems, and knapsack-style 'choose items under a capacity constraint' problems.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'two strings', 'grid', 'capacity', 'weight limit', 'subset sum'.
patterns.complexity: Typically O(n*m) time and space, sometimes reducible to O(m) space via rolling rows.

problems.name: Pascal's Triangle
problems.hint: Each row is built from the row above it: row[j] = prev[j-1] + prev[j].

problems.name: Unique Paths
problems.hint: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1] — number of ways to reach each grid cell.

problems.name: Minimum Path Sum
problems.hint: dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

problems.name: Longest Common Subsequence
problems.hint: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if chars match, else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

problems.name: Longest Palindromic Substring
problems.hint: dp[i][j] = True if s[i]==s[j] and the substring inside (i+1, j-1) is also a palindrome.

problems.name: Coin Change II
problems.hint: dp[i][amount] = ways using the first i coin types — a 2D unbounded-knapsack recurrence.

problems.name: Partition Equal Subset Sum
problems.hint: 0/1 knapsack: dp[i][sum] = can we hit exactly `sum` using a subset of the first i numbers.

problems.name: Target Sum
problems.hint: Reframe as a subset-sum/knapsack problem on (total + target) / 2.

problems.name: Interleaving String
problems.hint: dp[i][j] = can s3's first i+j chars be formed by interleaving s1[:i] and s2[:j].

problems.name: Edit Distance
problems.hint: dp[i][j] = min edits to convert word1[:i] to word2[:j], combining insert/delete/replace transitions.

patterns.name: Math & Number Theory
patterns.short_description: Problems solved with direct mathematical reasoning — digit manipulation, GCD/primality, modular arithmetic, and geometry — instead of a general search/DP pattern.
patterns.when_to_use: When a problem's constraints hint at a closed-form or number-theoretic shortcut (digits, divisibility, primes, exponentiation) rather than search or DP.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'digits', 'prime', 'divisible', 'power of', 'GCD/LCM', or an O(1)/O(log n) expected complexity that no search structure would give you.
patterns.complexity: Highly problem-dependent; often O(log n) (e.g. fast exponentiation, GCD) or O(n log log n) (e.g. Sieve of Eratosthenes for primes) rather than O(n) search-based approaches.

problems.name: Fizz Buzz
problems.hint: Basic modular arithmetic: check divisibility by 3 and 5 for each number.

problems.name: Palindrome Number
problems.hint: Reverse the number mathematically (via %10 and //10) and compare to the original.

problems.name: Sqrt(x)
problems.hint: Binary search for the largest integer whose square doesn't exceed x.

problems.name: Excel Sheet Column Number
problems.hint: Treat it as base-26 conversion, but with digits 1-26 instead of 0-25.

problems.name: Greatest Common Divisor of Strings
problems.hint: The answer's length is gcd(len(str1), len(str2)) — verify via the Euclidean algorithm.

problems.name: Reverse Integer
problems.hint: Pop digits with %10/ate//10, push into result, checking for 32-bit overflow at each step.

problems.name: Pow(x, n)
problems.hint: Fast exponentiation by squaring: halve the exponent each recursive step.

problems.name: Integer to Roman
problems.hint: Greedily subtract the largest matching value/symbol pair from a precomputed table.

problems.name: Count Primes
problems.hint: Sieve of Eratosthenes: mark multiples of each prime starting from p*p.

problems.name: Max Points on a Line
problems.hint: For each point, hash other points by slope (as a reduced fraction via gcd) to find the largest collinear group.

patterns.name: Design / Advanced Data Structures
patterns.short_description: Combine simpler structures (hash maps, doubly linked lists, heaps, arrays) to build a custom data structure meeting specific operation-complexity requirements — the most 'systems-flavored' DSA pattern.
patterns.when_to_use: 'Design a ...' problems specifying required time complexity for multiple operations (get/put/insert/delete), often needing two structures working together.
patterns.recognition_tips: Keywords: 'design', 'implement a class supporting', explicit O(1) or O(log n) requirements per operation across multiple methods.
patterns.complexity: Varies by design; the goal is almost always O(1) or O(log n) per operation, achieved by pairing a hash map (fast lookup) with a linked list/heap/array (fast ordering).

problems.name: Design HashMap
problems.hint: Array of buckets, each a list of (key, value) pairs; resolve collisions by scanning the bucket.

problems.name: Design HashSet
problems.hint: Same bucketing idea as Design HashMap, storing just keys.

problems.name: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
problems.hint: Array for O(1) random access + hash map of value -> index; swap-with-last to delete in O(1).

problems.name: LRU Cache
problems.hint: Hash map + doubly linked list: map gives O(1) lookup, the list gives O(1) reordering/eviction.

problems.name: Design Twitter
problems.hint: Hash maps for follows/tweets-per-user, merged with a heap to get the k most recent tweets across followees.

problems.name: Time Based Key-Value Store
problems.hint: Hash map of key -> list of (timestamp, value) sorted by time; binary search for the latest value <= a query timestamp.

problems.name: Design Underground System
problems.hint: Hash map tracking each in-progress check-in, plus running (total time, count) per route for averages.

problems.name: LFU Cache
problems.hint: Hash map to a node plus a hash map of frequency -> ordered list of nodes at that frequency (like LRU per frequency bucket).

problems.name: All O`one Data Structure
problems.hint: Doubly linked list of frequency buckets, each holding a set of keys, plus a hash map of key -> bucket.

problems.name: Design Skiplist
problems.hint: Layered linked lists with randomized 'express lane' promotion, giving expected O(log n) search/insert/delete.
